binding_record_note: Exactly Exchange and move-assignment declarations for each ordered family, joined to compiler-emitted callback methods. Native self-assignment is represented by the existing explicit assign_self route; these partial records grant no global parity credit.
changes: Added exchange_with, exchange_self_with and move_assign_with for both families, sharing the canonical table graph exchange introduced by the policy constructor batch.

The injected policy callback runs first. Completed policy swapping transfers the actual bucket/node/order graph, registry and allocator without reallocating, cloning, moving or destroying payload objects.
Direct native std::swap probes cover move construction, first move assignment and second move assignment failure prefixes, including temporary policy destructor traces and partial moved-from states.
All throwing prefixes preserve both original graphs, table/node addresses, allocators, extents and insertion order. Successful ordered move assignment exchanges both maps without Clear.

Native empty-graph bucket selection and existing self-assignment no-callback behavior are tested for both families. Native self Exchange still performs all three policy swap phases, including their distinct throwing prefixes; exchange_self_with reproduces this without aliasing mutable references.

Noncopyable native payloads/policies and non-Clone Rust payloads/policies prove the operations require no Clone or Default bound. Allocator leases remain live until owned nodes are destroyed exactly once.
Safe detached cursors stay valid on policy callback failure and reject moved-node transplantation after success. No raw iterator or cursor contracts were widened.
Existing callback-free exchange and move_assign remain compatible and explicitly document their Rust policy-swap semantics.
limitations: This is a scoped partial Exchange/move-assignment port, not class-wide or workspace API parity.

Rust has no implicit user-defined move constructor or assignment. The caller-provided swap callback must reproduce the native hasher policy operations; existing callback-free methods intentionally do not invoke those operations.
Injected closures may diverge from std::swap semantics; evidence covers the precise tested native policy domain rather than all arbitrary callbacks.

Native self-aliasing assignment is represented by assign_self and native self Exchange by exchange_self_with because two aliasing mutable references cannot be supplied safely. The self callback must implement the concrete native hasher self-swap behavior.

C++ conditional noexcept termination differs from Rust panic propagation and remains an unresolved domain. Native fixtures use throwing move/assignment policies, so tested native operations are not noexcept.
Safe detached cursors remain map-owner validated and cannot be transplanted to the receiving map, unlike native raw iterators. The non-owning registry transfers with graph ownership.
Default/copy constructor sequencing and partially constructed copy node lifetimes remain pending exact-behavior work; this batch grants no acceptance exemption for native retained-node failure paths.
Arbitrary raw bucket mutation, set safe FirstNode unit views, other forwarding/destruction policies and exact allocator handle reference-count observations remain separately tracked.
Scoped native/compiler/Miri evidence does not replace whole-workspace validation or global API/test completeness certification.
